title: [bug] Go tests launch full ralph loop in CI
description: CI test output shows ralph's actual log output ('=== PHASE 2: EXECUTION ===', 'All tasks complete\!', 'Stop file detected'). Unit tests are somehow triggering the full ralph orchestrator instead of testing functions in isolation. This is dangerous — ralph could modify the CI environment, create worktrees, push to remote. Tests must be pure unit tests that never launch the full loop with real git repos or real Claude processes. Find and fix the test that calls main() or runs the full loop without proper stubbing.
close_reason: Made Config.Runner required in loop.New() — tests must inject a stub, production passes real claude.Runner. PR #109.

title: [bug] CI tests fail: missing embedded prompts and git default branch mismatch
description: Two CI failures: (1) go/cmd/ralph/prompts/ is gitignored — CI can't build cmd/ralph because the embed directory doesn't exist. Fix: either run scripts/rebuild-go.sh in CI before tests, or stop gitignoring the prompts copy and commit it. (2) Git tests create repos with git init which defaults to 'master' on CI systems without init.defaultBranch=main. Tests then push to 'main' which doesn't exist. Fix: add 'git -c init.defaultBranch=main init' in test helpers, or detect the default branch name.
notes: Fix this first — CI broken means no PR can pass checks, blocking all auto-merges. ralph-rjr is likely same root cause. ralph-4tt second (prompt fix already committed). ralph-t47 third (functional but ugly).
close_reason: Fixed both CI failures: added prompts copy step in CI workflow for go:embed, and added -b main to all git init calls in test helpers. PR #110.

title: [bug] Orphaned tail processes accumulate — stream output multiplied
description: Each iteration spawns a new 'tail -f' process via startTail but never kills the previous one. Over an overnight run, dozens of tail processes accumulate, all writing to stdout. This multiplies every line of output. The cleanup code in Run() calls stopProcess(tailCmd) but tailCmd only references the LAST tail started — previous ones are leaked. Fix: kill the tail process at the END of each Run() call, and ensure the stream filter bash process is also killed. Currently ~50 orphaned tail processes running across ralph and tabi.
notes:
Bash ralph handles this correctly in run_claude (ralph.sh lines 962-1072): tail_pid and filter_pid are tracked as locals, then explicitly killed with pkill -P (kill children) + kill + wait at the end of every run_claude call. Each iteration cleans up its own processes before returning. The Go version must do the same — kill tail and stream filter processes at the end of each Run() call, not just on final cleanup.
Still accumulating — 15 orphaned tail processes after a few hours of running. This makes the log output completely unreadable. The fix in PR #107 didn't work. Must kill tail and stream filter processes at the end of each Run() call, matching bash ralph's cleanup pattern (lines 1064-1072 of ralph.sh).

title: [bug] Push fails after auto-merge deletes remote branch
description: With single-branch strategy, ralph reuses ralph/project/next for all tasks. But auto-merge passes --delete-branch to gh pr merge, which deletes the remote branch after squash. The next task's push fails because the remote branch is gone. Fix: either (1) don't pass --delete-branch in single-branch mode since the branch will be reused, or (2) after PostMergeReset, push with -u to recreate the remote branch. Option 1 is simpler. This is specific to single-branch — stacked mode creates a new branch per task so deletion is expected.
notes: Confirmed: ralph passes --delete-branch on line 414 of git.go. GitHub repo setting is false — it's ralph doing the deletion. For single-branch mode, remove --delete-branch from the gh pr merge command since the branch is reused.
close_reason: Omit --delete-branch from gh pr merge in single-branch mode. Extracted ghMergeArgs helper that conditionally includes --delete-branch only for stacked strategy. Also removed --delete-branch from shell auto_merge_current_branch.

title: [bug] Worktree doesn't pull latest main on resume
description: When ralph resumes in an existing worktree, it should rebase onto the latest origin/main. The user synced local main with remote before running ralph, but the worktree still had stale commits. The rebase step exists but may be using local main (which was stale) instead of fetching origin/main first. Verify the resume path does: (1) git fetch origin main, (2) rebase worktree onto origin/main. This is the root cause of the 'merge commit cannot be cleanly created' failures.
close_reason: Fixed: added explicit git fetch origin/main in tryResumeWorktree (Go) and setup_worktree resume path (shell). Also switched RebaseOntoDefaultBranch fetch from gitCmd to gitCmdErr so failures are logged. Added test proving refs are updated on resume.

title: [bug] Ctrl-C does not stop Ralph in tmux mode
description: Pressing Ctrl-C in tmux mode has no effect — produces ^C characters but does not stop Ralph or kill Claude. The user has to close the terminal and manually kill orphaned processes/tmux sessions. This is the highest-friction issue in daily usage. The signal handler must: (1) catch SIGINT on first press, (2) kill the Claude child process, (3) clean up state, (4) kill the tmux session, (5) exit. In tmux mode, the signal may be going to the wrong process group. Investigate whether the Go binary needs to use process groups or setsid for proper signal delivery. Affects both bash and Go versions but Go is primary.
notes:
This was previously tracked as ralph-anv. Ralph itself claimed to fix it and closed the bead, but the fix clearly didn't work — Ctrl-C still has no effect in tmux mode. The previous close reason is unknown (bead was lost). When ralph picks this up, it must actually verify Ctrl-C works in a real tmux session before closing.
THIS BUG HAS BEEN FALSELY CLOSED THREE TIMES. Each time ralph claimed to fix it via context threading or signal handling changes, but Ctrl-C still does not work in tmux. The fix MUST be verified by actually running ralph in tmux mode and pressing Ctrl-C. Do not close based on code review alone.
Additional issue: the interactive rebase recovery prompt (promptRebaseRecovery) uses fmt.Scanln which blocks and ignores Ctrl-C. The user gets stuck at 'Choice [1/2/3]:' with no way to exit. The prompt needs to handle SIGINT or use a context-aware reader.
close_reason: Verified: Ctrl-C message shows and ralph exits gracefully. Works from any point in lifecycle — tested during setup, rebase, and execution. User confirmed.

title: [bug] Go: Auto-merge not firing — multiple tasks stacking on single branch
description: Both branch strategies (single and stacked) must share the same completion path: (1) create PR for the task's commits, (2) push and open the PR. If --auto-merge: (3) squash-merge into remote main, (4) pull to local main, (5) rebase/reset worktree to latest main for next task. This is the same flow regardless of whether commits are on a shared branch or a per-task branch. The difference between strategies is only how branches are named and rotated, not the PR/merge lifecycle. Currently single-branch skips PR creation and auto-merge between tasks, stacking everything into one PR.
notes: Gate: PR creation and auto-merge must only proceed if all tests pass. This is a hard prerequisite — no PR should be created or merged with failing tests. Run full test suite after task completion, before the PR/merge flow.
close_reason: Fixed auto-merge for both branch strategies: PostMergeReset resets worktree to origin/main after each squash-merge, PushAndCreatePR ensures Go loop owns push/PR lifecycle rather than delegating to Claude, signal-gated flow fires push/PR on completion and auto-merge when enabled. PR #97.

title: Evolve mode: verify and fix --auto-improve end-to-end
description: Evolve (--auto-improve) exists but has known issues: (1) was wiping .ralph state on restart — fixed but needs test, (2) untested end-to-end: merge → pull → rebuild → exec cycle. Verify the full cycle works: task completes, PR merged, main pulled, binary rebuilt, ralph exec's itself and resumes execution (not planning). Add integration tests. Do NOT rename the flag — that is tracked separately in ralph-al6.
notes:
Implementation: use Unix exec syscall to replace the current ralph process with the rebuilt binary. exec preserves PID, stdin/stdout/stderr, and terminal attachment — the screen stays alive and output continues seamlessly from the new binary. This is why --evolve is incompatible with --tmux: ralph creates the tmux session, so exec'ing would lose tmux management. Without tmux, ralph is just a process in the terminal and exec works cleanly. Future: tmux support would require splitting into a supervisor process that manages tmux and an inner process that does work.
Guard: --evolve must verify the project is the ralph repo itself (e.g. check for go/cmd/ralph/ or ralph.sh). Error with a clear message if used on a non-ralph project — evolve only makes sense when ralph is iterating on its own code.
Bug: autoImproveRestart calls safeRemoveRalphDir which clears .ralph state. The new process starts fresh and enters interactive planning instead of resuming execution. Fix: do NOT clear .ralph on evolve restart — state must persist so it resumes where it left off. Only clear signal files between iterations, not the entire state directory.
IMPORTANT: Split out the flag rename from --auto-improve to --evolve as the LAST subtask. The user is actively running ralph with --auto-improve. Renaming the flag mid-run would break the current session. Do all other fixes first, rename last.
close_reason: Renamed --auto-improve to --evolve throughout codebase, added ralph repo guard (checks go/cmd/ralph/), added tests for guard and state preservation, fixed pre-existing IdleTimeoutProgress test default. All 17 test packages pass.

title: Simplify to one branch strategy: fresh branch from origin/main per task
description: REMOVE all branch strategy configuration. One opinionated workflow: (1) fresh branch from origin/main per task, (2) work + commit, (3) tests pass → push + create PR + squash-merge, (4) force-reset worktree to origin/main, (5) next task. Remove: --branch-strategy flag, --auto-merge flag (merge is always on), BranchStrategy config field, BranchSingle constant, all single-branch code paths, branch_strategy from ralph.toml. Auto-merge is the default and only behavior. Evolve compatibility: silently ignore stale branch_strategy and auto_merge values in state.json/ralph.toml.
notes:
Evolve compatibility: when the binary is replaced via --evolve, the old state.json may contain branch_strategy=single. The new binary must handle this gracefully — ignore unrecognized values and default to the only strategy. No crash, no error. Same for ralph.toml if it has the old config key. Just silently drop it. This should be implemented as part of this task, not a separate bead.
General principle for evolve: config must be forward-compatible. Unknown keys are ignored, removed keys use defaults. Never error on stale config. This applies to state.json, ralph.toml, and CLI args. A breaking change should degrade gracefully — the binary should always be able to start and run, even if the config was written by an older version.
Merge strategy depends on auto-merge mode: with auto-merge, squash-merge (clean history, force-reset after). Without auto-merge, regular merge (preserves commit history so stacked branches can rebase). Ralph should pass --squash or --merge to gh pr merge accordingly. The user's GitHub repo setting for default merge strategy should be respected as a fallback.
Squash-only repos (most of the user's repos) cannot have stacked dependent PRs — squash always breaks dependent branches. With auto-merge: solved by force-reset. Without auto-merge: only one outstanding PR at a time. Ralph must either (1) wait for user to merge before creating next PR, (2) just commit locally without pushing/PRing until user is ready, or (3) require auto-merge for squash-only repos. Option 2 is simplest — ralph works locally, user runs 'ralph push' or similar when ready to create PRs.
Without auto-merge workflow: ralph completes tasks locally but only pushes/PRs one at a time. After each task, push and create PR, then enter wait mode until the PR is merged (detect via polling gh pr view). Once merged, force-reset to origin/main and start next task. This gives the user review control while keeping ralph productive. The task manager can handle correction requests on open PRs.
Conclusion: auto-merge is not optional for ralph loop — it's required for squash repos (which is most repos). Default --auto-merge to on. Detect squash-only repos via gh api and warn/error if auto-merge is off. Without auto-merge, ralph loop is just a single-task runner that defeats its purpose — use 'ralph task' instead for manual workflows.
Correction: ralph task is bead management only, not a single-task executor. Without auto-merge in squash repos, there is no useful ralph loop mode — just use regular Claude Code directly. ralph loop requires auto-merge. Remove --auto-merge flag entirely and make it the default behavior. If the repo can't auto-merge (no gh, no permissions), error on startup.
Final workflow: worktree with thematic name, multiple tasks, each task creates a PR with related commits, squash-merge, force-reset to main, next task. No manual merge option. Codebase safety relies on: (1) all tests must pass before merge, (2) CI gates if configured, (3) git tags per task for easy revert, (4) user can ralph stop and review PRs on GitHub anytime. If tests are insufficient to catch regressions, that's a test coverage problem — ralph should flag low coverage areas.
close_reason: Splitting into smaller explicit tasks

title: Fix Go test mismatches: all Go tests must match unmodified bats tests exactly
description:
The Go migration cannot be considered complete until every Go unit test matches the exact behavior of its corresponding bats test. The bats tests are the source of truth — the Go implementation must be fixed to pass them, never the other way around.

## Mismatches to fix

### Analyzer (analyzer_test.go)
- configurable stagnation threshold: Go only tests config storage, bats tests that the threshold actually changes analyzer halt behavior. Add integration test.

### Git/worktree (git_test.go)
- Initial branch assertion uses HasSuffix instead of exact match ralph/project/next
- Branch rename test uses different task title input — must use Fix auth bug to get 01-fix-auth-bug
- Resume restores task_seq from state.json — Go uses branch count instead. Must match bats: restore from state.json with assertion == 2
- Dirty working tree: must test init_ralph_dir error behavior (status 1, uncommitted changes message), not just internal HasUncommittedChanges()
- rename_worktree_from_theme fallback: must test fallback logic with mocked backend, not just direct function call
- rename_worktree_from_theme preference: must test state.json theme preferred over bd task title with mocked backend

### Feedback (server_test.go)
- clear_feedback: missing test for deleting feedback file

### Stream filter (tmux_test.go)
- Deduplication: bats tests x3 counter logic for consecutive identical lines. Go does not test this at all.

### Auto merge (merge_test.go)
- Missing: skip when no PR exists (return 0, No open PR found)
- Missing: --auto-merge flag parsing in CLI

### Plan validation (config_test.go)
- Plan format validation tests are in wrong file or missing entirely
- Must test: nonexistent plan file exits with error, plan without checkboxes rejected, valid plan accepted

## Principle
The bats tests are the acceptance criteria for the migration. Write Go tests that assert the same inputs produce the same outputs. If a Go test fails, fix the Go implementation — do not modify the test to match existing Go behavior.
close_reason: Fixed all Go test mismatches against bats acceptance criteria: exact branch match, task_seq persistence, auto-merge support, plan validation, stream filter dedup, theme rename fallback. PR #79.

If stop file exists, skip evolve entirely and exit gracefully. This is a one-line check before the evolve code runs.

title: [bug] Ralph treats unknown positional args as directory names
description: Running 'ralph task' or any unrecognized word as a positional argument gets silently treated as the --dir argument, creating orphan directories (e.g. /ralph/task/ with its own .ralph and .beads). Anything else should error with usage help, not silently create a directory.

description: When ralph evolves (exec's itself with new binary): (1) print a bold, colored full-width separator line (e.g. bright magenta ═══════ RALPH EVOLVED ═══════) before the restart so the boundary between old and new binary is unmissable in scrollback, (2) show the rebuild-go.sh output (version being built, install confirmation) so it's clear the binary was rebuilt and we're running the new one. title: [bug] In-progress task takes priority over higher-priority ready tasks
description: When a task is in_progress, get_next_task returns it regardless of priority. If a P0 bug is created while a P3 feature is in_progress, ralph continues the P3 instead of switching. Do NOT preempt mid-task — that risks mixing changes on the same branch. Instead: (1) finish the current iteration, (2) on next task selection, compare priorities and pick the highest, (3) if the in_progress task wasn't completed (no signal, no commits), reopen it before selecting the next task. The in_progress check should only resume a task if nothing higher priority exists.
close_reason: Fixed priority-blind task selection: getNextIssue now compares priorities between in-progress and ready queues, preempting lower-priority in-progress tasks when higher-priority ready tasks exist. Reopens preempted tasks via bd update --status=open. Both Go and shell implementations fixed with full test coverage.

title: [bug] Stop file not deleted on clean exit
description: When ralph detects the stop file, it logs 'Stop file detected - halting' and exits, but the stop file persists. On the next start, ralph immediately detects it and exits again. The stop file should be deleted as part of the clean exit path — after detecting it and deciding to halt, remove it so the next launch starts fresh.

title: Fetch and rebase onto latest main between tasks, not just on resume
description: Superseded by simplified branch strategy (ralph-kjk). With auto-merge: force-reset to origin/main after each merge — no fetch/rebase needed, always fresh. Without auto-merge: stack branches on previous task's HEAD — each PR depends on the previous, user merges in order. The fetch-between-tasks concern is resolved by force-reset in auto-merge mode, and is irrelevant in no-auto-merge mode (stacked branches don't need latest main). Close once ralph-kjk is implemented.
notes: Integrate git-rebase-continue (~/.local/bin/git-rebase-continue) for handling non-trivial rebases. It already handles: auto-staging and continuing until a conflict needs manual resolution, --ours for specific files, --rm for files that keep reappearing, --auto for mechanical conflicts (add/add where theirs is a superset). Ralph should use this instead of bare git rebase for inter-task rebases — most rebase failures are mechanical and git-rebase-continue can resolve them automatically.
close_reason: Redundant: new strategy force-resets to origin/main after every merge. No rebase between tasks needed.

title: [bug] Last task's work not pushed/merged before entering wait mode
description: After the last task completes, ralph must still push, create PR, and squash-merge before entering wait mode or exiting. Same flow as every other task — no special case for 'last task'. The force-reset after merge is optional here since there's no next task, but the push/PR/merge must happen.

title: [bug] Single-branch stacks all tasks into one PR when merge fails
description: With single-branch strategy, all task commits go on ralph/project/next. After each task, ralph pushes and tries to merge. If merge fails (CI, conflicts), the branch keeps accumulating commits. The next task's push adds more commits to the same open PR. Result: one giant PR with all tasks instead of one per task. Fix: even when auto-merge fails, ralph must still create a NEW PR for the next task. Options: (1) create a new branch per task even in single-branch mode (effectively becoming stacked), (2) after failed merge, reset to main and cherry-pick only the new task's commits, (3) force-create a new PR by renaming the branch. This is distinct from ralph-8iu (rebase conflicts on resume) — this is about task isolation within a run.
close_reason: Resolved by dropping single-branch strategy entirely (ralph-kjk). All tasks now get fresh branches from origin/main.

title: [bug] Go: No Claude stream output in inline (non-tmux) mode
description: The Go stream filter (extractStreamText) can't parse Claude's stream-json format. It expects simple 'content':'string' but the actual format has 'content':[{'type':'text','text':'...'},{'type':'tool_use',...}] — nested arrays and objects. extractJSONString only handles flat key-value pairs. The bash version uses jq to navigate the nested JSON properly. Fix: either use encoding/json to parse properly, or port the bash jq filter logic. This blocks all non-tmux output — no Claude activity is visible in inline mode.
notes: Quick fix deployed: writes the bash stream filter script in inline mode and shells out to it. Works but duplicates the script between tmux.go and claude.go. Proper fix: either extract the script to a shared location, or rewrite extractStreamText to properly parse nested JSON with encoding/json.
close_reason: Replaced extractJSONString string-matching with encoding/json struct unmarshalling. extractStreamText now properly parses Claude's nested message.content[] array format. Tests updated to use actual stream-json format.

title: [bug] Rebase conflicts on resume after auto-merge squash
description: On resume, ralph rebases the worktree onto main. But after auto-merge squash-merges PRs, the worktree branch has original commits that conflict with the squash-merged versions on main. PostMergeReset should prevent this by resetting to origin/main after each merge, but it's not working reliably — the worktree still has stale commits on the next resume. May be a state persistence issue: the worktree branch stored in state.json points to the pre-reset branch.
close_reason: Fixed via PR #104 (squash merge of PRs 99-104). is-ancestor arg order corrected in git.go.

title: Replace --dangerously-skip-permissions with scoped permissions
description: Claude is launched with --dangerously-skip-permissions which gives unrestricted filesystem access. This allowed Claude to create an orphan directory named after a task ID (ralph-qut/) at the project root with its own .beads database. Fix in phases: (1) Near-term: use --allowedTools with directory-scoped restrictions to limit writes to worktree and .ralph only. (2) Medium-term: run each Claude iteration in a container (macOS 26 native 'container' CLI or Docker) with only the worktree mounted read-write. Full isolation, no filesystem leaks, reproducible environment. Consider making container mode the default for --auto-merge and --evolve.
close_reason: Phase 1 complete: replaced --dangerously-skip-permissions with --allowedTools in PR #104. Container isolation tracked separately.

title: Feed forward reflections and attempt history between tasks
description: Always feed the previous task's reflection to the next task, regardless of whether it's the same bead or a retry. Currently reflections are keyed by bead ID and only read on same-bead retries — which almost never happens because the agent rarely signals failure (it false-closes instead). Feed forward the 'what went wrong' and 'what could have gone better' sections from the last N reflections (e.g. last 3) to every new task. Universal learnings like 'run rebuild-go.sh before tests in worktrees' benefit all tasks, not just retries.
notes:
When a task is killed due to idle timeout, the next iteration must receive context about what happened: which task was being worked on, that it was killed for idle timeout (no output for 5m), and guidance to consider a lighter approach or make incremental progress rather than deep-thinking without output. This should be part of the attempt history fed forward — not just failures, but timeouts too.
Generalize: any analyzer action that kills/halts a task (idle timeout, stuck loop, stagnation, permission denial, repeated error) should write the reason into the attempt history. The next iteration receives: task ID, what was attempted, how it was killed, and the analyzer's reason. This lets Claude adjust its approach — e.g. avoid the same stuck pattern, use a different strategy, or break the work into smaller steps.

title: [bug] Ctrl-C requires multiple presses and leaves inconsistent state
description: Ctrl-C has no effect in tmux mode — both bash and Go versions. Pressing it repeatedly produces ^C and ^G characters but does not stop Ralph or kill Claude. The user has to close the terminal window and manually kill orphaned processes/tmux sessions. This is the highest-friction issue in daily usage. The signal handler must: (1) catch SIGINT on first press, (2) kill the Claude child process, (3) clean up state (close in-progress beads, write state), (4) kill the tmux session, (5) exit. In tmux mode, the signal may be going to the wrong process group — tmux may be intercepting SIGINT before it reaches the ralph process in pane 0. Investigate whether the Go binary needs to use process groups or setsid to ensure proper signal delivery.
close_reason: Fixed: check _interrupted flag in run_claude polling loop and execution loop so Ctrl-C breaks out on first press. Added graceful-then-force kill pattern for Claude process and writes interrupted status for resume.

title: ralph task — interactive task manager mode
description: Standalone subcommand: 'ralph task' launches Claude interactively with a task management prompt. NOT the execution loop. Separate code path: (1) print 'Task management mode', (2) inject beads context (open beads, recently closed, project state), (3) launch Claude interactively with prompts/task-manager.md, (4) exit cleanly when Claude exits — no worktree, no iteration loop, no planning phase. Two modes: light triage (default — quick bead CRUD, concise) and hands-on fix (when explicitly asked or blocking). Handles screenshots by describing visuals and saving to .ralph/screenshots/{bead-id}-{NN}-{slug}.png. Echoes back created beads for user review. Must use bd commands correctly: create with --deps, state what changed on updates, create dependencies programmatically not in notes.
notes:
Learning: never combine 'do X now' and 'consider Y later' in the same bead. These must be separate beads with a dependency. A multi-phase task gets closed when phase 1 is done, losing the future phases. Instead: create one bead per phase, link with --deps. The task manager prompt must enforce this — if the user describes a multi-phase approach, split it into separate beads immediately.
Learnings from live tabi task management session (2026-03-22):

**Status-check before bead updates**: Before updating any bead, check if it's closed. If it was falsely closed (no evidence the described work exists or doesn't match spec), reopen it, state why it was falsely closed, and define acceptance criteria for properly closing it. If legitimately closed and user is asking for new/different work, create a new bead. Use best judgement — don't prompt the user.

**Accumulate across messages, deduplicate across beads**: When user adds details to a feature they mentioned earlier, find the existing open bead and append rather than creating a new one. Scan for duplicates before creating.

**Priority inference defaults**: Infer from context — don't ask every time. Bugs are inherently higher priority than features at the same level.
- P0: Blocking — ralph can't run, build broken, critical path completely blocked
- P1: Broken functionality (bugs), broken UX
- P2: Non-critical bugs, missing features the user explicitly asked for
- P3: Nice-to-haves, research, polish, feature requests without urgency

**Audit mode**: A way to verify recently closed beads — check if described functionality actually exists and matches spec, report mismatches. Reopen false closes with acceptance criteria stating what needs to be true to properly close.

**Two-way sync awareness with ralph loop**: Task manager should know loop is running in parallel. When creating P1 bugs, note that loop may pick them up. When the user says 'fix this now', the task manager handles it directly in hands-on fix mode rather than waiting for loop.
CRITICAL: the task manager must NEVER start ralph loop, run ralph commands, or launch nested terminal processes. It manages beads only. Starting ralph from within the task manager would create invisible nested terminals. The task manager prompt must explicitly forbid this.
Must integrate with bd states (ralph-sh2): the task manager should be able to query task states (bd state ralph-xxx), challenge closes that skipped the verified phase, and set states manually when triaging (e.g. marking a falsely-closed task as phase=unverified when reopening).
close_reason: Breaking down into discrete subtasks

Fix: pass --subject to gh pr merge to force the PR title as the squash commit message. Format: '[ralph-xxx] PR title (#N)'. Ensures git log on main is readable and matches the PR history.

title: Show task priority with color in log output
description: When ralph logs the current task (e.g. 'Next task: ...'), include the priority and color it: P0 red, P1 orange/yellow, P2 yellow, P3 green, P4 dim/grey. Format: '[beads] Next task: [P0] Force-reset worktree...' with the priority tag colored. Applies to both the ralph pane log and the stream pane signal detection output.

title: Add post-rewrite hook to rebuild Go binary after pull --rebase
description: The post-merge hook rebuilds the Go binary but doesn't fire on git pull --rebase (which uses post-rewrite instead). Add a post-rewrite hook that calls scripts/rebuild-go.sh so the binary is rebuilt regardless of pull strategy. Update scripts/setup-hooks.sh to install both hooks.

title: Highlight signal file writes in stream output
description: When Claude writes to signal files (.signal_current_task, .signal_complete, .signal_all_complete), these lines appear as regular [Bash] echo commands in the stream. They should be visually distinct — highlighted yellow with a [signal] prefix — since they mark task boundaries (pickup, completion). The stream filter should detect writes to .signal_* paths and format them differently from normal Bash output.

title: [bug] Ralph pane title overwrites Claude's /rename of iTerm window
description: Claude uses /rename to set the iTerm terminal window title, which is useful for identifying sessions. But ralph's pane title updater overwrites it back. Ralph should either: (1) not set the terminal title at all and let Claude's rename persist, (2) incorporate the renamed value, or (3) only set the tmux pane border title and leave the terminal window title alone. The iTerm window title and tmux pane title are separate — ralph should manage the pane border, Claude manages the window title.

title: ralph task: detect and break down unwieldy beads
description: The task manager should detect when a bead is accumulating too many notes or covering multiple concerns, and proactively suggest splitting it into discrete subtasks with acceptance criteria and dependencies. Rule of thumb: if a bead has more than 3 distinct concerns in its description/notes, it should be split.

title: ralph task: integrate bd states for lifecycle tracking
description: Task manager queries task states (bd state), challenges closes that skipped verified phase, sets states when triaging (e.g. phase=unverified when reopening falsely-closed tasks).

title: ralph task: screenshot handling for visual bugs
description: When user provides screenshots, describe the visual issue and save to .ralph/screenshots/{bead-id}-{NN}-{slug}.png. Include text description and path in the bead. The fixing agent reads the image via multimodal Read.

title: ralph task: echo back created beads for review
description: After creating a bead, show the ID, priority, type, title, and full description so the user can review and amend. Short descriptions in full, long ones truncated.

title: Group same-timestamp log lines under one timestamp
description: When multiple log lines arrive at the same timestamp (e.g. a multi-line PR body or Claude's thinking), they each get their own timestamp prefix, making the output noisy and hard to read. Group lines with the same timestamp: show the timestamp once, then indent continuation lines. E.g. '13:02:16 [claude] First line\n          Second line\n          Third line' instead of repeating '13:02:16' on every line.

title: Run Claude iterations in macOS native containers
description: Run each Claude iteration inside a macOS 26 native container (container CLI) for full filesystem isolation. The worktree is mounted read-write, everything else is read-only or inaccessible. Prevents Claude from creating orphan directories, running bd init in wrong locations, or modifying files outside the worktree. This is the proper solution for autonomous operation — --allowedTools scopes tool permissions but doesn't restrict filesystem access. Depends on macOS 26 Tahoe shipping the container CLI.

title: ralph command — four-pane tmux with loop + task manager
description: Launches full four-pane tmux layout: top-left is ralph loop, bottom-left is ralph task (interactive task manager), top-right is stream, bottom-right is plan. Implies --tmux. All flags (--auto-merge, --evolve, --wait, etc.) pass through to the loop pane. The task manager pane stays alive independently for user interaction while the loop runs.

title: ralph review — post-mortem mode to integrate reflection learnings
description: Reflections are written per-bead and only fed forward if the same bead is retried. Learnings are lost when beads are closed/reopened or replaced. 'ralph review' should: (1) scan all reflections in .ralph/reflections/, (2) extract common patterns and recurring issues, (3) surface actionable learnings that should be added to AGENTS.md or prompt templates permanently, (4) show reflections from falsely-closed beads. Could also cross-reference reflections with reopened beads to identify systemic issues (e.g. 'ralph keeps closing beads without verifying').

title: Show current task ID in log line prefix
description: In inline (non-tmux) mode, the log lines show timestamps but no indication of which task is being worked on. Add the current bead ID after the timestamp: '12:55:48 [ralph-5iv] [Read] /path/...' instead of '12:55:48 [Read] /path/...'. The task ID comes from the .signal_current_task file or state. In tmux mode this is already visible in the stream pane title, but inline mode has no equivalent.

title: Store screenshots for visual bugs in .ralph/screenshots/
description: When the task manager receives a screenshot for a visual bug, save it to .ralph/screenshots/{bead-id}-{NN}-{slug}.png (e.g. tabi-e2b-01-wrong-license-copy.png, tabi-e2b-02-settings-panel.png) with zero-padded two-digit numbering for sort order. The slug is a short kebab-case summary of what the screenshot shows. Multiple screenshots per bead are numbered sequentially. The agent picking up the task can read the images via Claude's multimodal Read tool to see the actual visual issue. The task manager should also include a text description alongside each path. Screenshots dir should be gitignored.

title: Task manager: echo back created bead for user review
description: After creating a bead, ralph task should echo back the ID, priority, type, title, and full description so the user can review and amend before moving on. E.g. show the bead summary and ask 'Looks good? (enter to confirm, or type changes)'. Currently the user has to run bd show to verify what was created. Short descriptions show in full, long ones truncated with option to expand.

title: Show reflection summary in log output
description: After writing a reflection, ralph just logs 'Writing reflection'. Show the first line or a truncated summary of the reflection content so the user can see what was learned without opening the file. E.g. 'Reflection: Fixed is-ancestor arg order — was comparing HEAD to main instead of main to HEAD'.

title: Install script with homebrew dependencies for Go ralph
description: Create an install script for Go ralph that handles all dependencies. Homebrew installs: bd (beads), gh (GitHub CLI). Go toolchain for building from source. No longer needs: jq (Go uses encoding/json), bash-specific tools. The install script should: (1) check/install homebrew deps, (2) clone from agent-skeleton template if new, (3) build the Go binary, (4) symlink or copy to ~/.local/bin/ralph, (5) run scripts/setup-hooks.sh. This is for when Go ralph fully replaces bash ralph and becomes the sole implementation.

title: Remove checklist backend — make beads the only task backend
description: The checklist backend (plan.md with markdown checkboxes) was a fallback when bd wasn't available. It doubles the maintenance surface: every feature needs dual implementations, tests diverge, and the checklist path gets less attention. Beads provides everything checklist does plus dependencies, priorities, types, labels, close reasons, history, and audit trail. Make bd a hard requirement. Remove: checklist_* functions from lib/tasks.sh, checklist.go, execution-checklist.md prompt, --plan-file flag, TASK_BACKEND switching logic, all checklist tests. The fallback-to-checklist code path in bd_init can become a hard error instead.

title: ralph command — four-pane tmux with loop + task manager
description: 'ralph command' launches the full four-pane tmux layout: top-left is ralph loop, bottom-left is ralph task (interactive task manager), top-right is stream, bottom-right is plan. Implies --tmux. 'ralph loop' and 'ralph task' can also run standalone without tmux. 'ralph command' is the recommended way to run ralph — full visibility and control. All flags (--auto-merge, --evolve, --wait, etc.) pass through to the loop pane. The task manager pane stays alive independently for the user to interact with while the loop runs.
notes:
Tmux layout: split pane 0 (ralph) horizontally. Top-left: ralph loop output. Bottom-left: ralph task interactive session. Right side (stream + plan) unchanged. Launch both together with 'ralph --tmux' which starts the loop in top-left and task manager in bottom-left. The task manager pane stays alive independently — user can interact with it while the loop runs.
'ralph commander' launches the full four-pane tmux layout with both loop and task manager. 'ralph loop' and 'ralph task' can also run standalone.
The task manager prompt should set expectations for speed: quick triage, concise responses, create/update beads and move on. Do not deep-dive into code, explore the codebase, or attempt fixes unless explicitly asked. The user is reporting issues in real-time while ralph loop runs — the task manager needs to keep up, not block on research. Light task management, not engineering.
Two operating modes: (1) Light triage (default): quick bead creation, updates, audits. Concise responses, don't explore code unless asked. (2) Hands-on fix: when the user explicitly asks to fix something now, or when an issue blocks ralph loop from running at all. In this mode, read code, make fixes, run tests, commit. The prompt should make the default mode clear but not prevent switching to fix mode when needed.
Current state: 'ralph task' subcommand exists but is wired to the normal planning/execution flow. It needs a completely separate code path: (1) print 'Task management mode', (2) launch Claude interactively with prompts/task-manager.md, (3) exit cleanly when Claude exits — no execution phase, no worktree, no iteration loop. Currently broken — shows Phase 1 planning and falls into execution.
When the user provides screenshots, the task manager should describe what it sees and include that description in the bead. Do not store screenshots in beads — they're text-based. Note the screenshot path in the bead if needed for reproduction. The task manager prompt should instruct Claude to verbally describe visual issues from screenshots.
Depends on ralph-aus (ralph task) being complete first. ralph command integrates ralph loop + ralph task into a four-pane tmux layout — it can't work until both modes exist independently.
Learnings from live tabi task management session (2026-03-22):

**Echo back every bead creation with full description**: User needs to see exactly what was captured. Show ID, priority, type, title, and full description after every create/update. Don't make them run bd show. (See ralph-xbs.)

**Always check issue status before updating**: Never update a closed issue — create a new one or reopen first. The task manager hit this repeatedly: piling requirements onto tabi-1es which was already closed by a merged PR.

**Verify closed issues aren't falsely closed by ralph loop**: Ralph loop auto-closes beads after writing code, but the code may not match the spec. Task manager should have an audit mode: pull closed issues, verify against codebase, reopen mismatches. We had to reopen 13 issues in one session.

**Screenshot handling**: User pastes DOM + screenshot. Task manager describes the visual issue in the bead description since beads are text-only. Include site URL. For DOM problem mode bugs, follow the AGENTS.md DOM PROBLEM MODE flow (simplified DOM, verify understanding, TDD test, fix).

**Accumulate related requirements on one bead**: User often adds details to a feature across multiple messages. Task manager should update the existing open bead rather than creating duplicates. But NEVER update closed ones.

**Smart priority inference**: P1 for broken functionality, P2 for missing features and UX issues, P3 for nice-to-haves and research. User shouldn't have to specify priority every time.

**Cross-project awareness**: Task manager should know which project it's in (from cwd) and use the right bd database. When user references other projects (e.g. Ralph issues from tabi context), use --db flag.

**Hands-on fix mode**: When user says 'fix this now', switch from triage to engineering. Read code, make the fix, run tests, commit, push. Then switch back to triage mode. The keybinding fix (B=batch, M=marks) was done this way mid-session.

**Don't create bd issues for things already in AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md**: These are static instructions, not tasks. Only create beads for work that needs doing.
RETRACTION: 'Cross-project awareness' note above is wrong. Task manager should be fully isolated to its project directory. No --db flag usage, no reaching into other project databases. The user (human) bridges across projects, not the agent.

title: Replace repeated-tool-call stuck detection with better heuristics
description: The current stuck detection counts repeated tool+target pairs per iteration (5+ triggers). This produces false positives during normal development — reading the same file 5 times in one iteration is routine. Remove this heuristic and replace with more reliable detection: (1) no git diff + no new commits + completion signal = suspicious, (2) same task picked up N consecutive iterations without progress, (3) Claude explicitly says it's blocked. Repeated tool calls across a session (not consecutive) are not meaningful — only consecutive identical calls in a tight loop indicate actual stuck behavior. The stagnation detector (no-change across iterations) already catches the real stuck case.

title: Error normalization in response analyzer
description: Extract error lines from Claude output (Error:, Failed:, Exception:, panic:, non-zero exit codes). Normalize by stripping timestamps, UUIDs, line numbers, temp paths, collapsing whitespace. MD5 fingerprint normalized errors. Track in .ralph/.error_hashes per task. Threshold: same fingerprint 3x → trigger per-task skip. Clear fingerprints on task change.
close_reason: Implemented error normalization and fingerprinting in response analyzer. Extracts error lines, normalizes by stripping volatile parts, MD5 fingerprints them, tracks per-task in .ralph/error_hashes. Same fingerprint 3x triggers halt:repeated_error and task skip. PR #71.

title: Deprecate ralph feedback in favor of ralph task + beads
description: ralph feedback injects text into the next iteration's prompt — no persistence, no tracking, no verification. It does NOT interrupt the current iteration; it's picked up on the next one. This is identical to creating a bead, which also gets picked up on the next iteration. Beads are strictly better: persistent, tracked, auditable, can be reopened, have priority. There is no use case where feedback adds value over ralph task + beads. Remove feedback entirely rather than deprecating.

title: Filter escape sequences from stream pane output
description: Arrow key presses in tmux panes produce ^[[A/^[[B escape sequences in the stream output when the pane process (tail -f) doesn't consume them. Filter these out in the stream filter script so they don't clutter the logs. Could also set the pane to read-only or disable input forwarding for panes 1 and 2 since they're display-only.
close_reason: Added stty -echo to stream filter and plan watcher scripts (Go + shell) to suppress terminal escape sequences in display-only tmux panes. Tests added for both.

title: Review git tag naming for task start/end markers
description: Ralph creates tags like 'ralph/task-ralph-ner/start' and 'ralph/task-ralph-ner/end' to mark task boundaries. The naming is redundant (ralph appears twice) and the tags themselves may not be useful — the information is already in beads and git history. Consider removing tags entirely or simplifying to 'task/ralph-ner/start' if they serve a purpose.
close_reason: Simplified task tag naming from ralph/task-{id}/{suffix} to task/{id}/{suffix}, removing the redundant ralph prefix. Tags are kept since they provide useful task boundary markers in git history.

title: Revisit auto-merge feature after single-branch implementation
description: The auto-merge feature (ralph-67p) may be redundant once we switch from stacked branches to single worktree branch with one-shot commits. After implementing the single-branch approach, evaluate whether auto-merge is still needed or if it should be removed. The stacked branch model needed merging between tasks; a single branch may not.
close_reason: Auto-merge is still needed: stacked branches (one per task) are still used. Wired --auto-merge through Go loop (calls AutoMergeCurrentBranch after task signals) and resume script. PR #88.

title: Go: Handle squash-merge rebase failures gracefully
description: When rebase fails due to squash-merged branches, Ralph should prompt the user with options: (1) create a fresh worktree from current main (delete old worktree, clear state, keep beads), (2) manually resolve conflicts, (3) abort. Currently it just halts with an error. The fresh worktree option is almost always what the user wants since completed work is already on main via squash merge.
close_reason: Added RebaseConflictError type, RecreateFromMain method, and OnRebaseConflict handler callback. When rebase fails, the loop consults a configurable handler offering fresh worktree, manual resolve, or abort options. CLI wires up an interactive prompt. 6 new tests cover all recovery paths.
